steps.note: HARD-WRAPPED (REAL source: this plan's own § Change list) — seven items whose lines wrap with a three-space indent, no blank lines: ONE list, 1-7

delta.text:
1. **Marker regex**, on already-escaped text (safe: markers are `-*+` and digits): `LI_RE = /^( {0,3})([-*+]|\d{1,9}[.)])( {1,4}|$)(.*)$/`. Content indent `W` = indent + marker length + spaces (spaces capped at 4; `$` case → marker + 1). Type = ul/ol; `start` = the first item's number. 2. **Item collection** from the marker line: take the rest of the line, then subsequent lines while they are (a) blank, (b) indented ≥ W (strip W), or (c) LAZY: non-blank, previous collected line non-blank, and not a block start (`LI_RE` at indent < W, heading, hr, quote, fence placeholder, table-at). Stop on a same-type `LI_RE` at indent < W → next item; anything else at indent < W → list ends. Trailing blank lines are dropped; a blank line between items or between an item's blocks marks the list **loose**. 3. **Render items recursively**: `mdBlocks(itemLines.join('\n'), blocks, tight)` — the same re-entry the blockquote branch already uses, so nested lists, tables and fence placeholders inside items come free. New third parameter `tight`: the paragraph branch emits its text bare (no `

`) when tight; nested lists decide their own tightness. Loose items keep `

`. 4. **Emit** `

    ` when N ≠ 1 (`
      ` otherwise), `
        ` for bullets. Placeholders inside items resolve because de-indenting by W leaves the exact ` B ` line. 5. **Fence indent strip** in the fence callback: from the match `offset`, measure the whitespace between the line start and the opener; drop up to that many leading spaces from each body line (CommonMark) so a code block indented under `1. ` does not render with three leading spaces. The placeholder keeps the line's indent in front of it — that is what the list parser de-indents. 6. **Paragraph branch**: stop condition uses `LI_RE` instead of the old `([-*+]|\d+\.)\s` test. 7. **CSS** `webview/css/30-blocks.css` next to `.blk li { margin: .2em 0; }`: `.blk li > p { margin: .25em 0; }` (loose-item paragraphs tighter than body paragraphs; same em idiom as the surrounding rules — no new token). Nested lists already inherit `.blk ul, .blk ol` padding.
